c.tagline: Peru's City of Eternal Spring, ringed by adobe empires and surf-town sunsets.

taxi.fareNote: Most Trujillo taxis are unmetered; agree the fare before getting in, or use a ride app for a fixed price. Short trips in the center run a few soles.

emergency.note: 105 reaches the Peruvian National Police; 116 is the SAMU medical emergency line. 911 is not standard in Peru.

avoid.reason: Elevated crime; caution in the centre and El Porvenir district

hood_desc: Trujillo's colonial core around the Plaza de Armas, full of pastel casonas, wrought-iron window grilles, churches, museums, restaurants and nightlife; the best base for first-timers who want everything walkable.

A laid-back Pacific surf-and-fishing town about 12 km northwest, famous for its long promenade, ceviche shacks, reed caballitos de totora boats and a World Surfing Reserve; ideal for travelers who want beach time over city bustle.

A central, well-connected residential urbanization just off the main avenues, close to clinics, universities, shopping and mid-range hotels; a convenient, safer-feeling base a short ride from the historic center.

An upscale, leafy district of gated urbanizations like El Golf and California near the coast, with modern apartments, malls and the city's smartest hotels and restaurants; suits travelers wanting comfort and calm.
A breezy coastal neighborhood in Víctor Larco with a wide beach, seafood spots and sunset walks; a quieter local alternative to Huanchaco, popular with residents on weekends.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not reliably potable.

transit.hours: City micros and combis run roughly 5:30 AM to around 11:00 PM; late-night travel relies on taxis and ride apps.
transit.note: Trujillo has no metro or rail. Public transport is a dense web of privately-run micros (small buses) and combis (shared minibuses) that connect the center with Huanchaco, Chan Chan, Moche and the districts, supplemented by taxis and ride-hailing apps.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver or cobrador on board (roughly S/1-2 within the city, a little more to Huanchaco). There is no unified transit card. Keep small change handy.
